name: bicarbonate-buffer
caption: The bicarbonate buffer couples rapid pulmonary CO2 removal to slower renal H+ excretion and bicarbonate reabsorption.
alt: Reversible CO2 hydration and carbonic acid dissociation, with carbonic anhydrase on the hydration step, lungs removing CO2, and kidneys excreting H+ while returning bicarbonate.

name: protein-structure-levels
caption: Protein structure progresses from amino-acid sequence through local secondary structure and a folded chain to assemblies of multiple subunits.
alt: Four panels show an amino-acid chain with N and C termini, an alpha helix and beta sheet with hydrogen bonds, one folded chain with a disulfide bridge and hydrophobic core, and a two-alpha two-beta tetramer.

name: hemoglobin-t-r
caption: Hemoglobin shifts between the low-affinity T state favored by tissue conditions and the high-affinity R state favored by oxygen loading in the lungs.
alt: Two alpha-two beta tetramers show 2,3-BPG between the beta chains in the deoxy T-state cavity and four bound oxygen molecules in the compact R state, joined by opposing loading and unloading arrows.

name: collagen-synthesis
caption: Collagen is modified and assembled as procollagen inside fibroblasts, then cleaved and cross-linked extracellularly into fibrils.
alt: A fibroblast contains sequential hydroxylation, glycosylation, triple-helix formation and secretion; extracellular peptidases and copper-dependent lysyl oxidase produce cross-linked fibrils. Disease tags identify scurvy, osteogenesis imperfecta, Ehlers–Danlos and Menkes.

name: electron-transport-chain
caption: Electron transport across the inner mitochondrial membrane, proton pumping, ATP synthesis, inhibitors, and uncoupling.
alt: Complexes I and II donate electrons through CoQ, III, cytochrome c, and IV to oxygen. I, III, and IV pump protons into the intermembrane space. ATP synthase and an uncoupling channel allow proton return to the matrix.

name: carbohydrate-metabolism-map
caption: Glucose-6-phosphate links glycogen turnover, the pentose phosphate pathway, glycolysis, and gluconeogenesis.
alt: A glucose-6-phosphate hub connects glucose, glycogen, the pentose phosphate pathway, glycolysis and pyruvate oxidation. A coral return pathway carries pyruvate through oxaloacetate and PEP toward glucose.

name: lipid-digestion-absorption
caption: Dietary triacylglycerol is digested, absorbed, re-esterified, and exported in chylomicrons through intestinal lymph.
alt: A left-to-right diagram shows bile emulsification, pancreatic lipase and colipase, monoacylglycerol and fatty acids, mixed micelles, enterocyte re-esterification, apo B-48 chylomicrons, and a lacteal.

name: carnitine-shuttle-beta-oxidation
caption: The carnitine shuttle transports long-chain fatty acyl groups into the mitochondrial matrix for β-oxidation.
alt: Fatty acid activation and CPT-I on the outer membrane feed acylcarnitine to an inner-membrane translocase and matrix-facing CPT-II. Matrix β-oxidation proceeds through FAD-dependent oxidation, hydration, NAD+-dependent oxidation, and thiolysis, yielding acetyl-CoA.

name: lipoprotein-metabolism
caption: Exogenous and endogenous lipoprotein transport, receptor uptake, and HDL-mediated reverse cholesterol transport.
alt: Intestinal chylomicrons receive apolipoproteins from HDL and become remnants cleared by the liver. Liver VLDL passes through IDL to LDL for receptor uptake; HDL collects peripheral cholesterol and returns it to liver, with LCAT and CETP shown.

name: urea-cycle
caption: The urea cycle links mitochondrial carbamoyl phosphate formation to cytosolic urea production and regeneration of ornithine.
alt: CPS I activated by N-acetylglutamate forms carbamoyl phosphate in the mitochondrion. OTC produces citrulline, which enters the cytosolic cycle with aspartate and ATP, forming argininosuccinate, arginine, fumarate, urea and returning ornithine.

name: heme-degradation-bilirubin
caption: Heme breakdown, hepatic bilirubin conjugation, and intestinal conversion to fecal and urinary pigments.
alt: Macrophages break heme into biliverdin, releasing iron and carbon monoxide; biliverdin becomes unconjugated bilirubin, which travels bound to albumin to liver for glucuronidation. Biliary conjugated bilirubin enters intestine, producing urobilinogen, stercobilin and urobilin, with enterohepatic recycling.

name: replication-fork
caption: A bacterial replication fork showing continuous leading-strand synthesis and discontinuous lagging-strand synthesis, both in the 5′ to 3′ direction.
alt: A left-moving fork opens parental DNA on the left. The upper daughter grows continuously left toward the fork, while lower Okazaki fragments grow right. Topoisomerase, helicase, single-strand binding proteins, primase, DNA polymerases III and I, and ligase are labeled with antiparallel strand ends.

name: mrna-processing
caption: Eukaryotic pre-mRNA receives a 5′ cap, undergoes intron splicing, and gains a 3′ poly(A) tail before nuclear export.
alt: A eukaryotic gene is transcribed by RNA polymerase II. Processing caps the 5′ end, removes introns as lariats, joins three exons, and adds a 3′ poly(A) tail before mature mRNA passes through a nuclear pore.

name: translation-ribosome
caption: Eukaryotic translation uses the 40S and 60S ribosomal subunits, with tRNAs moving through A, P, and E sites as the ribosome reads mRNA 5′ to 3′.
alt: A 60S large subunit above a 40S small subunit surrounds mRNA oriented 5′ left to 3′ right. E, P, and A sites contain an exiting empty tRNA, a peptidyl-tRNA carrying a chain, and an incoming aminoacyl-tRNA. eEF1, peptidyl transferase, eEF2, and downstream termination are annotated.

name: lac-operon
caption: The lac operon is repressed without lactose, strongly expressed when lactose is present and glucose is low, and weakly expressed when both sugars are present.
alt: Three aligned lac-operon diagrams show lacI, CAP site, promoter, operator, lacZ, lacY, and lacA. Repressor blocks the operator without lactose. Allolactose releases repression in both lactose conditions, while cAMP–CAP binds only when glucose is low.

name: pcr-cycle
caption: A PCR cycle denatures DNA, anneals two inward-facing primers, and extends new strands with Taq DNA polymerase.
alt: Three clockwise PCR steps show denaturation at 94–95 °C, annealing at 50–65 °C, and extension at 72 °C. Antiparallel templates receive primers with inward-facing 3′ ends. Taq extends each complementary strand 5′ to 3′, producing two duplexes.

name: central-dogma
caption: DNA information is transcribed into mRNA, translated, and expressed as protein and phenotype.
alt: DNA in a nucleus has a replication loop and a mutation note. Transcription makes mRNA, which exits to a cytoplasmic ribosome for translation into polypeptide, folded protein, and phenotype.

name: atp-coupling
caption: ATP couples energy released by catabolism to biosynthesis, transport, and muscle work.
alt: Fuel breakdown releases energy for ATP synthesis from ADP and phosphate. Adenine, ribose, and three phosphates compose ATP, whose hydrolysis powers assembly of small molecules into a macromolecule. Listed ATP uses include biosynthesis, transport, and muscle work.

name: co2-transport-bohr
caption: Tissue CO2 transport and the chloride shift reverse in the lungs; lower pH and higher CO2 reduce hemoglobin oxygen affinity.
alt: Paired red blood cells show carbonic anhydrase reactions, H+ buffering by deoxyhemoglobin and tissue O2 release. Tissue bicarbonate efflux and chloride influx reverse in the lungs, with O2 binding, H+ release, and CO2 exhalation.

name: sickle-hbs
caption: The β-globin Glu-to-Val substitution promotes deoxy-HbS polymerization, sickling, hemolysis, and vaso-occlusion.
alt: A DNA-to-protein row highlights β-globin position 6, followed by red cells showing deoxy-HbS polymer fibers and sickling. Consequences include hemolysis and obstructed vessels causing pain crises. Blue notes state that oxy-HbS does not polymerize and hydroxyurea increases HbF and reduces polymerization.

name: lysosomal-targeting-m6p
caption: N-linked glycosylation and mannose-6-phosphate tagging direct lysosomal enzymes from the rough ER through the Golgi to lysosomes.
alt: A glycan assembled on dolichol transfers to protein asparagine in rough ER. Golgi phosphorylation creates the mannose-6-phosphate sorting signal for receptor-mediated vesicle transport to lysosomes. An I-cell disease inset shows missorted secreted enzymes and lysosomal inclusions.

name: ketogenesis
caption: Ketone body synthesis in liver mitochondria and use by extrahepatic tissues.
alt: Fatty acid β-oxidation supplies acetyl-CoA for HMG-CoA synthase and acetoacetate production. Acetoacetate interconverts with β-hydroxybutyrate or forms exhaled acetone. Ketones travel to brain during prolonged fasting, heart and muscle for acetyl-CoA and the TCA cycle. The liver lacks thiophorase, and excess ketones cause high anion gap metabolic acidosis.

name: fatty-acid-synthesis
caption: Cytosolic fatty acid synthesis and regulation of acetyl-CoA carboxylase.
alt: Mitochondrial citrate is exported to cytosol and converted to acetyl-CoA, then by biotin-dependent acetyl-CoA carboxylase to malonyl-CoA. Fatty acid synthase uses NADPH to produce palmitate (16C). Insulin activates ACC, glucagon and AMPK inhibit ACC, and malonyl-CoA inhibits CPT-I to block β-oxidation.

name: eicosanoid-pathways
caption: Arachidonic acid pathways and the targets of glucocorticoids, NSAIDs and aspirin.
alt: Phospholipase A2 releases arachidonic acid from membrane phospholipid and is inhibited by glucocorticoids. COX-1 and COX-2 produce prostaglandins, platelet thromboxane A2 and prostacyclin; NSAIDs and aspirin inhibit COX. Lipoxygenase produces leukotrienes associated with bronchoconstriction.

name: cholesterol-synthesis-statins
caption: Cholesterol synthesis, reductase inhibition and the effect of statins on LDL clearance.
alt: Acetyl-CoA leads to HMG-CoA, which HMG-CoA reductase uses with NADPH in the rate-limiting step to mevalonate and subsequently cholesterol. Statins, cholesterol feedback and AMPK phosphorylation inhibit the reductase. Statins increase hepatic LDL receptors and LDL clearance.

name: ldl-receptor-cycle
caption: LDL receptor recycling, cholesterol feedback and unregulated scavenger uptake.
alt: ApoB-100 on LDL binds an LDL receptor in a clathrin-coated pit. Endocytosis delivers LDL to an acidic endosome, the receptor recycles and LDL is degraded in lysosomes to free cholesterol, which decreases HMG-CoA reductase and LDL receptor synthesis. Defective LDL receptors cause familial hypercholesterolemia with high LDL and early atherosclerosis. Macrophage scavenger receptors take up oxidized LDL without downregulation, forming foam cells.

name: insulin-secretion
caption: Glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and proinsulin processing.
alt: Glucose enters a pancreatic beta cell via GLUT and is metabolized after glucokinase, increasing ATP/ADP, closing KATP channels, depolarizing the membrane and opening voltage-gated calcium channels. Calcium influx triggers insulin granule exocytosis. Preproinsulin becomes proinsulin, then insulin plus C-peptide, which marks endogenous insulin.

name: fed-fast-fuel-flow
caption: Organ fuel handling in fed and fasting states.
alt: Parallel fed and fasting panels show liver, adipose, muscle, brain and red blood cells. High insulin relative to glucagon favors hepatic glycogen and fat synthesis, adipose TAG storage, muscle glycogen and protein synthesis, and glucose use by brain and RBC. Low insulin relative to glucagon favors hepatic glycogenolysis then gluconeogenesis, adipose lipolysis, muscle fatty acid use, brain glucose then ketones, and continuing RBC glycolysis.

name: dna-repair-pathways
caption: Mismatch, nucleotide excision and base excision repair compared.
alt: Three columns show mismatch repair cutting out and resynthesizing a stretch of the new strand, nucleotide excision repair removing an oligonucleotide containing a bulky UV thymine dimer, and base excision repair removing a small damaged base by glycosylase, creating an AP site and replacing one nucleotide. All use the intact complementary strand. Lynch syndrome and xeroderma pigmentosum identify associated repair defects.

name: srp-protein-targeting
caption: Signal-directed targeting to the ER, nucleus and mitochondrion.
alt: SRP recognizes an emerging signal sequence on a free ribosome, pauses translation and docks at an ER SRP receptor. The cytosolic ribosome feeds protein through a translocon into the ER lumen, where signal peptidase removes the signal. Side panels show a retained nuclear localization signal at the nuclear pore and a mitochondrial amphipathic targeting sequence passing through TOM/TIM. Free and ER-bound ribosomes are identical; signals determine targeting.

name: blotting-and-cloning
caption: Blotting methods and the plasmid cloning workflow.
alt: Gel separation is followed by membrane transfer and probe detection. Southern detects DNA with a DNA probe, Northern detects RNA with a DNA probe, and Western detects protein with antibody. Restriction enzymes cut vector and insert at sticky ends, ligase seals a recombinant plasmid carrying a labelled origin of replication, antibiotic-resistance marker and cloning site, and bacteria are transformed and selected.
